6                 IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                    
7                     FOR THE DISTRICT OF ARIZONA                        

8                                                                        

9   Chad Huhn,                         No. CV-20-02437-PHX-DWL           

10              Plaintiff,              ORDER                             

11   v.                                                                   

12   Trevor Milton, et al.,                                               

13              Defendants.                                               
14                                                                        
15        The Court has reviewed the parties’ stipulation to again stay this action (Doc. 16) 
16   and  is  unpersuaded.   As  background,  this  shareholder  derivative  action  was  filed  in 
17   December 2020, more than three years ago, but was then stayed at the parties’ joint request 
18   due to its potential overlap with an earlier-filed securities class action, Borteanu v. Nikola 
19   Corporation et. al., No. 2:20-cv-01797-PHX-SPL (“the Securities Class Action”), which 
20   had been filed in September 2020.  In the stay request, the parties anticipated that the stay 
21   would remain in effect until the Securities Class Action was dismissed with prejudice or 
22   the defendants in the Securities Class Action filed an answer.  (Doc. 9.)  Thus, on January 
23   26, 2021, the Court ordered that this action was “stayed in its entirety until 30 days after 
24   the earliest of the following events: (a) [the Securities Class Action] is dismissed in its 
25   entirety with prejudice; (b) Defendants file an answer to any complaint in the Securities 
26   Class Action; or (c) Plaintiff and Defendants file a joint request to lift the stay.”  (Doc. 10.)  
27   The parties were ordered to “promptly notify the Court if either of the first two events 
28   occurs.”  (Id.)                                                      
1        On  January  26,  2024—three  years  to  the  date  after  this  action  was  stayed—
2   Defendants filed an answer in the Securities Class Action, such that the stay in this action 
3   expired 30 days thereafter, on February 26, 2024, as the parties acknowledge in their 
4   pending stipulation.  (Doc. 16 at 2.)  However, the parties did not “promptly notify the 
5   Court,” and therefore the stay, which had already expired, was never formally removed 
6   from the docket.  The result of the parties’ failure to inform the Court was a de facto 
7   extension of the stay.  Indeed, Defendants have yet to respond to the complaint. 
8        The  parties  are  now  requesting  another  stay  because  a  separate  shareholder 
9   derivative action was filed in Delaware Chancery Court in 2022 and the parties believe that 
10   “future developments in the Delaware Chancery Action may have implications” for this 
11   action.  (Doc. 16.)                                                  
12        A stay is “not a matter of right,” but is rather “an exercise of judicial discretion,” 
13   the propriety of which “is dependent upon the circumstances of the particular case.”  
14   Virginian Ry. Co. v. United States, 272 U.S. 658, 672-73 (1926).  “The party requesting a 
15   stay bears  the  burden  of  showing  that  the  circumstances  justify  an  exercise  of  that 
16   discretion.”  Nken v. Holder, 556 U.S. 418, 433-34 (2009).  In the case of a joint motion, 
17   the parties share that burden.  In determining whether to grant a motion to stay, “the 
18   competing interests [that] will be affected by the granting or refusal to grant a stay must be 
19   weighed.”  Lockyer v. Mirant Corp., 398 F.3d 1098, 1110 (9th Cir. 2005) (citing CMAX, 
20   Inc. v. Hall, 300 F.2d 265, 268 (9th Cir. 1962)).                    
21        The Court “has an interest in managing judicial resources by preventing inactive 
22   cases from remaining indefinitely on its docket,” United States v. Grantham, 2018 WL 
23   3239938, *2 (S.D. Cal. 2018), and therefore the parties must demonstrate that other factors 
24   outweigh this interest to prevail in seeking a stay.  The Court does not foreclose the 
25   possibility that there may be a good explanation for requiring this 2020 case to remain 
26   stayed so that an overlapping shareholder derivative action filed in 2022 can proceed, but 
27   no such explanation appears in the parties’ stipulation.  Stating that “future developments” 
28   in the later-filed action “may have implications” for this action is too conclusory.  Thus, 
 1 ||  the stay request is denied without prejudice.  The parties may renew their stay request at 
2||    any time, but for now, the stay is lifted. 
3          Accordingly, 
4          IT IS ORDERED that: 
5          1.     The stay (Doc. 10) is lifted. 
6          2.     The stipulation (Doc. 16) is denied without prejudice. 
7          3.     Within 14 days of the issuance of this order, the parties may file a renewed 
8 ||  stay request.  If no renewed stay request is filed, Defendants shall respond to the complaint 
9||    within 28 days of the issuance of this order.  If a renewed stay request is filed, Defendants’ 
10 ||  deadline to respond to the complaint will be stayed pending the resolution of the renewed 
11 ||  stay request. 
12          Dated this 22nd day of March, 2024. 
13

                                                        Dominic W.  Lanza
